Q: Why windows refuses to execute this exe file A:

I have limited knowledge but one this is for sure I can tell is that If you only want ImageBase = 0x00400000 (no other changes), then Only change OptionalHeader.ImageBase. Please Do not touch:

AddressOfEntryPoint, BaseOfCode, BaseOfData , Section headers’ VirtualAddress and SizeOfRawData/PTR or Data directories (Import, IAT, Reloc)

I dont htink you can achieve this by turning RVAs into VAs. Rather you should focus on using a large empty section (BSS) to reserve address space.

At link time:

ml /c /coff test.asm
link test.obj kernel32.lib ^
  /subsystem:console ^
  /entry:START ^
  /base:0x00400000 ^
  /fixed:no ^
  /dynamicbase:no ^
  /nodefaultlib ^
  /section:.pad,UNINITIALIZED

Then provide a module (obj) that defines a large symbol in .pad (BSS) to make the linker emit a big VirtualSize without raw data:

; In a separate ASM file or the same one:
.data?            ; uninitialized data (.bss)
pad_reserve BYTE 400000h DUP (?)  ; reserve 4 MB (example)

If you can provide the key header fields from both files (ImageBase, AddressOfEntryPoint, BaseOfCode, BaseReloc, Import, and a section table dump), then may be we can help you better in identifying which field got turned into VAs and provide the precise values to restore.

Updated based on the comments

Kindly keep all addresses as RVAs in headers and import structures.

Optional Header: AddressOfEntryPoint = 0x401000, BaseOfCode = 0x401000, BaseOfData = 0x402000.

Section Headers: .text.VirtualAddress = 0x401000, .rdata = 0x402000, .data = 0x403000, .reloc = 0x404000.

Data Directories: - This part seems fine and consistent. Refer PE_FORMAT

Import Directory RVA = 0x40210C,

IAT Directory RVA = 0x402000,

Debug Directory RVA = 0x40200C,

Reloc Directory RVA = 0x404000 (size 0x14).

In your MASM grouping, the small IAT lives inside .rdata (flags IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ). The loader can still modify it (it can change page protections), but the conventional placement is .idata with IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE. If you move the idata groups into a dedicated .idata section or flip the section’s characteristics to include WRITE, you align with common practice and avoid rare protection edge cases. All of these structures like Data Directory entries, Import Descriptor fields, thunk arrays store RVAs. The loader computes the final VA as VA = ImageBase + RVA at load time. If you accidentally store VAs in those fields, the loader will add the ImageBase again and go to the wrong place.Your approach (huge RVAs) does create a large zero-filled region before your first “real” section, but Windows will still reserve that entire [ImageBase, ImageBase + SizeOfImage) range for the image. That means the memory is not available for other modules or allocations, even if no raw data maps there. If your broader goal is to keep 0x400000–0x800000 truly free for another component, you can’t achieve that by shifting RVAs inside one image; the loader always reserves the image contiguously. (Typical alternatives are separate modules, custom allocators after process start, or rebasing the other component.)

Kindly Run dumpbin /imports test1.exe , if it is giving output as

Import Address Table at 402000

Import Name Table at 402134

DLL name pointer near 402160
(all are RVAs and should be inside .rdata.)

Launch with CreateProcess or double‑click; it should now load and print “Test”.

Q: Set Initial View magnification to "Fit Page", "Fit Height" or "Fit Width" A:

Magnification is defined by a destination in the catalog’s /OpenAction
Fit Page → [page /Fit]

Fit Height → [page /FitV left]

Fit Width → [page /FitH top]

Page Layout is the catalog entry /PageLayout:

Single Page → /SinglePage

Navigation**:** “Show Bookmarks Panel and Page**”** is controlled by /PageMode:

Bookmarks panel → /UseOutlines

The page view is shown by default unless /FullScreen or another exclusive mode is used.
